transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-16
Time: 15:30 - 16:19 UTC
Duration: 49 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Evan Chu (Redwood CSM); Miguel Torres (CTO - Springboard), Aisha Khan (Head of MLOps), Samir Patel (SRE), Lina Park (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal/check-in to amend commitment for Q4, scope APAC pilot for private VPC/DC in Singapore, discuss failover routing and warm standby/latency SLAs, and align on benchmarks and procurement timeline.

Topics Covered:
- Current utilization and projected uplift
- Dedicated vs Hosted for APAC pilot
- Failover policies and regional routing
- Security/compliance asks (KMS, SOC2 evidence, audit logs)
- Pricing amendment: burst tiers and term extension
- Next steps and timeline for procurement

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to do a short check-in — mainly renewal and the APAC pilot ask that we saw in the email thread. can everyone hear okay?
[00:12] Miguel Torres (Springboard): Yep, loud and clear. thanks Jordan.
[00:15] Aisha Khan (Springboard): Hi all. quick heads up, we have a hard Q4 deadline for the Singapore pilot, and procurement wants the contract amendment lined up early.
[00:25] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Got it. Priya and I brought a scoped plan — we'll walk through utilization numbers, the suggested commit bump, and a failover playbook for region outages.
[00:34] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Thanks. So to start with, can we confirm the current steady-state tokens and peak burst shape? I pulled the telemetry you shared but wanted to validate.
[00:45] Samir Patel (Springboard SRE): Yeah, on average we're at about 1.2M tokens/day for the recommender flows, with peaks up to 6M on weekday batch runs — bursty for certain models.
[00:56] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Okay that matches what we saw. For Pegasus-lite model you referenced, what percent of traffic needs sub-200ms p95 latency?
[01:08] Miguel Torres (CTO): Roughly 30% of requests are user-facing and need low-latency. the rest can tolerate up to 800ms.
[01:18] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Good — that split helps. For the APAC pilot, we recommended a small Dedicated pool in Singapore for the low-latency slice, plus a hosted fallback in us-west for overflow. That lets you keep costs down while ensuring SLA for critical requests.
[01:35] Aisha Khan (Springboard): When you say fallback, do you mean automatic cross-region routing? how does that look if the Singapore cluster loses capacity?
[01:44] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Yes — Redwood's smart routing can fail over by policy. for example, route by priority: region, then cost tier, then model variant. we can set a max-allowed additional latency and only route overflow that still meets the p95 requirement.
[01:58] Samir Patel (Springboard SRE): there's still concern on bandwidth and egress costs if we route to us-west frequently — procurement will raise that.
[02:06] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Totally — that's why our proposed amendment has a tiered burst clause: small committed bump for APAC plus a capped burst allowance with usage-tiered pricing. we'll show numbers on the worksheet.
[02:18] Miguel Torres (Springboard): also need to confirm data residency for the user-facing slice — can logs or PII be kept in APAC only?
[02:27] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): For Redwood Private (we sometimes say Redwood private control plane), you can keep logs and KV caches within the VPC and choose KMS keys in region. audit logs can be retained in-region; we'll need to map what counts as PII in your schema.
[02:42] Aisha Khan (Springboard): Do you have SOC2 / ISO evidence we can pass to our security team?
[02:47] Evan Chu (Redwood CSM): Yes — we'll share the vetting pack. there's a SOC2 Type II report and the security questionnaire we've completed; I'll attach those in the follow-up.
[02:55] Lina Park (Procurement): timeline wise we need the PO path — will this be an amendment to the existing Master Services Agreement?
[03:02] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Yes, an amendment. we'll draft an exhibit that lists committed capacity, burst tiers, term extension to 12 months, and the pilot region clause.
[03:12] Samir Patel (Springboard SRE): technical question — what's the cold start for a Dedicated pool if we scale up on demand? we want to avoid a cold cache spike.
[03:22] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Dedicated nodes are warm by default for pinned models; for burst we have warm standby nodes and quick spin-up. cold start for a new instance is around 20–40s depending on model size, but with prefix/KV cache warming and continuous batching we can keep effective latency low for sustained load.
[03:41] Miguel Torres (CTO): you mentioned quantization profiles earlier — would switching to a lower-precision runtime change latency/cost materially?
[03:48] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Yes, quantization to int8 or q4_0 reduces memory and can improve throughput, but inference quality needs to be validated per-model. we'll run a quality check on your prompt set as part of the benchmark.
[03:59] [04:15] Speaker 2 (transcript artifact): uh mm-hmm
[04:18] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): For the benchmark checklist: we need 1) representative payloads 2) concurrency targets 3) p95/p99 targets 4) security constraints like KMS and VPC egress. I'll share the doc.
[04:32] Samir Patel (Springboard SRE): I'll get concurrency and payload examples. also we'll include the typical retry/backoff behavior.
[04:39] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Perfect. On routing and failover, one option is to reserve a small cross-region buffer — basically a low-cost reserved headroom in us-west that we only use if Singapore goes above X% utilization. cheaper than routing everything to hosted in the moment.
[04:58] Miguel Torres (CTO): Can you quantify X% and the cost? that's what finance will want.
[05:03] Jordan Lee (Redwood): We'll model a few scenarios in the pricing workbook — e.g., 10% buffer vs 25% buffer and show delta on monthly costs. that's in the action item to send by Monday.
[05:12] Aisha Khan (Springboard): On security: are we able to bring our own KMS? we need HSM-backed keys for key material.
[05:19] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Yes, for Private deployments and Dedicated with VPC integrations you can use customer-managed keys with supported KMS/HSM providers. the audit logs will show key usage events.
[05:29] Lina Park (Procurement): For the amendment, do we need to renegotiate support SLAs? we have a requirement for a 4-hour P1 response.
[05:36] Evan Chu (Redwood CSM): We can include a P1 response SLA as part of the enterprise support add-on. I'll outline options and uplift pricing in the worksheet.
[05:44] Miguel Torres (CTO): Any limitations on model variants per pool? we may want multiple versions pinned for canaries.
[05:51] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): You can pin multiple model versions, and we support canary rollouts with traffic splits. the Dedicated pool can host multiple pinned variants; we recommend sizing for peak token throughput across all pinned versions.
[06:05] [06:30] Speaker 1: hmm
[06:32] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): small note about KV cache: if you have long session flows, prefix caching will reduce repeat token cost significantly. that impacts the cost model — we'll include that assumption in the workbook.
[06:45] Samir Patel (Springboard SRE): Good, we'll estimate session lengths. also need to know retention windows for audit logs and tokenization traces for compliance.
[06:54] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Right. For compliance, we can do region-bound log retention and can export to your SIEM.
[07:01] Miguel Torres (CTO): One more thing — if we extend the term to 12 months do you offer any pricing credit for committed bump?
[07:08] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Yes, we typically provide step discounts for multi-month commits and a better rate for upfront billing. I'll outline a few commit tiers.
[07:18] Aisha Khan (Springboard): from an ops perspective, how disruptive is switching traffic to dedicated nodes? we want an orchestrated cutover.
[07:25] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): We can do staged cutover with canary traffic, traffic shadowing, and validation checks. cutover time depends on traffic shape but is usually non-disruptive if we plan warm caches and do small traffic ramps.
[07:37] [07:55] Miguel Torres (Springboard): ok that sounds fine. procurement wants an approval path — Lina will drive that internally.
[07:59] Lina Park (Procurement): Yep I will. also curious about the billing granularity for burst usage — hourly? daily?
[08:06] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Burst billing is hourly for Dedicated capacity and per-token for hosted overflow. we'll clarify the exact granularity in the worksheet.
[08:14] Samir Patel (Springboard SRE): on monitoring — will we get per-route traces and token-level cost breakdown?
[08:20] Evan Chu (Redwood CSM): Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token breakdown, and traces. we can also provide a longer retention package if you need history for audits.
[08:31] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): For the APAC pilot we recommend starting with a 3-node Dedicated pool sized for the low-latency slice and then add a burst reserve of 1-2 nodes that can be warm for traffic spikes.
[08:45] Miguel Torres (CTO): what's the expected lead time to provision Dedicated nodes in Singapore?
[08:51] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Provisioning is typically 5–7 business days for Dedicated in an existing region; if it's a new region or private on-prem, it takes longer. we'll confirm exact timelines in the follow-up.
[09:02] Samir Patel (Springboard SRE): we might need a SOC2 attestation and the network IP ranges for allowlist — can you include the CIDR blocks and firewall guidance?
[09:10] Evan Chu (Redwood CSM): We'll include the IP ranges, firewall guidance, and a security pack with SOC2 evidence.
[09:16] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Quick note — one competitive ask was around model telemetry retention — MosaicServe gives 90 days by default, is that something we should call out?
[09:25] Miguel Torres (CTO): Yes mention retention; we want 180 days for dev & audit teams.
[09:30] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): We can offer 180-day retention as an add-on. that will be in the pricing.
[09:36] [09:50] Speaker 3: yep
[09:52] Aisha Khan (Springboard): timeline check: pilot needs to start first week of November to hit Q4 customer betas. procurement wants contracts signed by Oct 7. is that feasible?
[10:02] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Oct 7 sign date is tight but doable if we move quickly — action items: Jordan to send amendment by Mon 9/20, Priya to run benchmarks by Fri 9/18, Springboard to send traffic sample by Tue 9/21.
[10:14] Miguel Torres (CTO): sounds good. any blockers on our side for the pilot config?
[10:19] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Not from Redwood; just need the payloads and target SLAs. we'll also need SSO SAML metadata for users who need admin access.
[10:30] Samir Patel (Springboard SRE): we'll provide SAML and our security contact.
[10:35] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): Great. I'll also include a short checklist for the pilot cutover and post-cutover validation tests.
[10:43] [11:05] Jordan Lee (Redwood): One operational thing — in case Singapore has a sustained issue, our recommendation is to fail traffic over to the buffer in us-west and set client-side retry windows to prefer region-local responses first. we can provide a default routing policy for you.
[11:19] Miguel Torres (CTO): acceptable. if failover increases latency by 150–200ms for non-critical flows that's ok. critical flows must remain below 300ms p95.
[11:31] Priya Raman (Redwood SE): We'll tune the policy to keep critical flows under that threshold where possible.
[11:37] Evan Chu (Redwood CSM): I'll attach the renewal worksheet and the support SLA options in the follow-up.
[11:44] Miguel Torres (CTO): any final asks from Redwood?
[11:48] Jordan Lee (Redwood): just confirmation of pilot region (Singapore), the committed bump number (we suggested +30% for the low-latency slice), and the sign-by date.
[11:58] Lina Park (Procurement): Procurement will aim to get approvals by Oct 6 if Jordan sends the amendment by Sep 20.
[12:06] Miguel Torres (CTO): We confirm Singapore for the pilot. we'll share traffic and SAML by Sep 21.
[12:12] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Perfect. Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the worksheet and the benchmark checklist.

Recap & Next Steps (verbatim):
- Jordan: draft amendment and pricing workbook (due 2026-09-20)
- Priya: run latency & quality benchmarks with sample payloads (due 2026-09-18)
- Samir: share traffic shape, concurrency targets, SAML metadata (due 2026-09-21)
- Lina: internal PO/approval path details (due 2026-09-23)

End of transcript.
